title: Weight Sanctum: conversion, certification, and stable-pin publish workflow
creator: Ava Chen
description: Implement an end-to-end certification pipeline ("Weight Sanctum") that takes community/open-source model weights from intake through deterministic conversion to Redwood runtime artifacts, runs functional and performance certification, and publishes a stable canonical pin and a performance profile to the model catalog. This task bundles the conversion worker, deterministic validation harness, perf-profiling job, canonical manifest generator, and automated publish step. Goal: reduce manual triage and time-to-catalog from days to hours while ensuring deterministic correctness and reliable runtime performance metadata.
acceptance_criteria: A converted runtime artifact (canonical .runtype) is produced for a variety of input weight formats (PyTorch, safetensors, HF Flax) with a reproducible conversion log
Automated deterministic validation suite passes: token-level generation parity on a curated set of prompts within 1e-4 for float models and semantically equivalent outputs for quantized variants
Performance profile is published with median latency (p50), tail latency (p95), max throughput for 1, 4, 8 batch sizes, peak GPU memory, and recommended quantization/tiling knobs
A canonical model manifest (model.json) is created and stored in artifact registry with a generated stable pin that can be used by the catalog and rollout systems
Rollback policy and fallback variant mapping are created automatically when performance or correctness regressions are detected
Pipeline emits structured telemetry and badges (compatibility, performance-grade, security-scan) visible in the Console model catalog page
steps: 1) Intake: adapter to fetch weight bundles from URLs/registry + signature/hash generation
2) Preflight: run format detectors, file integrity checks, and size/mmap heuristics
3) Conversion Worker: run deterministic conversion to Redwood runtime format with pinned toolchain; log kernels and quantization choices
4) Unit Validation: run deterministic prompts (seeded) and token-comparison harness; generate pass/fail artifacts
5) Profiling Stage: run perf harness across representative sequence lengths, batching, and kv-cache warmups (collect latency, throughput, memory)
6) Safety & Security Scans: run dependency checks, license scan, and binary sanitizer
7) Manifest Generator: synthesize canonical manifest with model metadata, compatible runtime versions, and recommended runtime knobs
8) Pin Publisher: create an immutable pin + variant list (fp16, int8, q4 variants) and publish to model catalog with profile
9) Post-publish smoke: light traffic against Hosted runtime to validate end-to-end serving and metrics collection
10) Notifications: create release note, update onboarding dashboard, and attach PRs/links
